best_for: Linux and Windows users who take screenshots for bug reports and docs and want to add arrows, blur and numbered steps before the image leaves the screen.
description:
Flameshot is a screenshot tool made by a volunteer team, the Flameshot contributors, who have worked on it in the open since 2017. You drag a box over the part of the screen you want, and the tools appear right around it.

Most actions are one key away. Arrow keys nudge the selection by a single pixel, and Shift with an arrow resizes it. The mouse wheel makes your pen thicker or thinner, and G grabs a color straight from the screen. When you are done, Ctrl+C copies the shot, Ctrl+S saves it, Ctrl+O hands it to another app, and Enter uploads it to Imgur. Ctrl+Z undoes a mistake, and Shift+Print Screen brings back your recent captures.

points.title: Annotate in the capture itself
points.text: After you drag a region you can add arrows, boxes, circles, text, highlights, freehand lines, blur or pixelation, and auto-incrementing numbered markers. Settings let you pick the buttons, colors, shortcuts and how captures are saved.

points.title: Scriptable from a terminal
points.text: Commands like `flameshot gui` run without opening the main window, so you can bind them to your own keyboard shortcuts or call them from scripts.

points.title: Wayland takes setup
points.text: On Wayland it captures through the desktop portal. GNOME 41 and later asks you to approve sharing on each capture, and missing `xdg-desktop-portal` packages can leave captures blank. The project's Wayland guide lists fixes for GNOME, KDE and Hyprland.

points.title: Mac install needs a manual approval
points.text: On first launch macOS may say the developer cannot be verified. The docs have you approve it under Privacy and Security, then grant screen recording permission. Homebrew has disabled its cask after it failed the Gatekeeper check, so use the DMG. The DMGs listed here, for Intel and Apple silicon, are marked for macOS 15 or later.

points.title: Free under GPL 3
points.text: Flameshot is free and open source under the GPL 3. All builds are 64-bit only.

points.title: Windows MSI and a verified Flatpak
points.text: Windows gets an x64 MSI that installs machine-wide, and this site keeps 14 Windows versions. The Linux Flatpak is verified on Flathub as published by the Flameshot developers. Mac and Linux list only the current release here, so downgrades there need another source.
